item.title: Said & Checked, Texas, 2026-11-23: none false or contradicted, 1 unsettled (Donald Trump)
item.description:
No statement was found false or contradicted.

Unsettled

  • Donald Trump, President of the United States: “I received a phone call two days ago from the new governor of -- governor-elect of Texas. She was really nice. It was a very productive call. And she wants to have a strong border.” Unsettled. Texas's governor-elect, Gina Hinojosa, told the Texas Tribune on Nov. 18 that she had called the president the previous Saturday, apparently Nov. 14, to discuss border security, and said he 'understands my commitment to keeping a secure border.' The date of the president's remarks was not established, so 'two days ago' can be neither confirmed nor ruled out.

item.title: Said & Checked, Texas, 2026-11-20: 1 contradicted (Chip Roy)
item.description:
False or contradicted

  • Chip Roy, U.S. Representative: “The empire is that which gave us the $42 trillion of debt” Contradicted. Treasury's Debt to the Penny series in AskAmerica's warehouse shows total public debt of $40.715 trillion on Nov. 17, 2026, about $1.3 trillion below $42 trillion. The Treasury source could not be read directly outside the warehouse.

item.title: Said & Checked, Texas, 2026-11-19: none false or contradicted, 1 unsupported, 4 unsettled (John Cornyn)
item.description:
No statement was found false or contradicted.

Unsupported and Unsettled

  • John Cornyn, U.S. Senator from Texas: “Reported as: Cornyn also said the White House has requested information about his preferred candidate, Fort Worth lawyer Steve Fahey.” Unsupported. No White House statement or other record of a request for information about Steve Fahey was found; the only accounts are Cornyn's and his aide's. The search covered AskAmerica's nominations data, the AP and HNGN reports, the Senate Judiciary Committee's nominations page and a web search; White House records not made public were not reachable.
  • John Cornyn, U.S. Senator from Texas: “Reported as: Texas Sen. John Cornyn told The Associated Press that he has not returned the "blue slip" for Elliot Gaiser, a top official at the Justice Department who was nominated for the Dallas-area vacancy earlier this month, nor does…” Unsettled. AskAmerica's nominations data show T. Elliot Gaiser's nomination (PN1505) referred to the Senate Judiciary Committee on Nov. 16, 2026; the committee publishes no per-nominee blue-slip record, and the only account of a withheld blue slip is Cornyn's own.
  • John Cornyn, U.S. Senator from Texas: “He's not from Texas. He hasn't been vetted.” Unsettled. AskAmerica's nominations data list the nominee as "T. Elliot Gaiser, of Ohio," and CBS reporting relayed by HNGN says his only apparent Texas tie is a one-year clerkship in Houston. On vetting, the AP reports Cornyn meant Texas's bipartisan judicial evaluation committee, while Cruz is reported as saying Gaiser has a completed FBI background check; "vetted" fits either reading, and the questionnaire was not read.

Disagreements

  • John Cornyn, U.S. Senator from Texas: “there's better qualified people to hold that job”
    Ted Cruz, U.S. Senator from Texas: “If the Senate Judiciary Committee does not move Gaiser forward, the people of Texas will pay the price because it will effectively give the judicial seat to the Democrats, who will keep it vacant in perpetuity”
    Both statements in context

item.title: Said & Checked, Texas, 2026-11-17: none false or contradicted, 1 unsettled (Dick Durbin)
item.description:
No statement was found false or contradicted.

Unsettled

  • Dick Durbin, U.S. Senator from Illinois: “He lost on Tuesday. On Wednesday, he learned that he is going to be a Federal district court nominee.” Unsettled. Texas Supreme Court Justice James Sullivan lost his Nov. 3 race; Reuters reported on Thursday, Nov. 5 that a Senate Judiciary questionnaire named him for the Western District of Texas, and the President announced the nomination on Nov. 10. No source read says when he learned of it.

item.title: Said & Checked, Texas, 2026-11-15: none false or contradicted, 1 unsupported, 1 unsettled (Sean Duffy)
item.description:
No statement was found false or contradicted.

Unsupported and Unsettled

  • Sean Duffy, U.S. Secretary of Transportation: “Reported as: In a post on the social media platform X, Duffy said contractor L3Harris Technologies Inc. had secured two routers from FAA facilities in Texas and Arkansas and was conducting "deep diagnostics" on the equipment.” Unsupported. The FAA names two sites, in Amarillo, Texas and El Dorado, Arkansas, and a new router at El Dorado, and says it and L3Harris are still investigating. Neither the FAA nor L3Harris says two routers were secured or that diagnostics are under way; the only source found for that is the secretary's post.
  • Sean Duffy, U.S. Secretary of Transportation: “When we turned that router on, we saw that in Amarillo, Texas, a system we had replaced about three weeks earlier, that started to flood our system as well.” Unsettled. The FAA's published Q&A names a radar site in Amarillo, Texas as one of two potential sources of the flooding, so a second site is part of the official account. It gives no date for when the Amarillo system was replaced, and the cause at both sites is still under investigation.
